creative.serviceTruth: Defined Detail professionally cleans and details vehicles in Telford, including everyday cars and supercars. The advert must show dirt being removed and a visibly clean car.
creative.audienceRecognition: After a proper detail, the first dirty drive feels like spoiling the finish. This fictional owner takes that affection to an unreasonable conclusion.
creative.visualStyle: Photorealistic British commercial photography. Warm side-window daylight balanced with soft white inspection lights. Natural skin, tactile water and paint, restrained sincere performances and dimensional light. No artificial star sparkles.
creative.continuity: The actual fictional cobalt-blue fixed-roof sports coupe from the selected acting take. Dark slender bright-edged wheel spokes, yellow brakecaliper, rounded newlyrevealed headlight, blue front-wing/bonnet contours. Same tall black-framed left window, grey block wall, upright and diagonal inspection lights. The matching wash/result were regenerated around this observed car; the previous different wheel set is excluded. Nose details were not visible in the dialogue frame and are a coherent fictional extension, not a verified real customer vehicle.

concepts.title: The taxi
concepts.firstFrame: A practical female detailer in a black polo holds the keys beside a spotless cobalt-blue sports coupe. Its grey-haired owner in ordinary sage overshirt and grey T-shirt has come to collect it. Medium two-shot, both faces and the gleaming bonnet prominent, in the same bright grey studio.
concepts.premise: At collection, the owner decides to take a taxi rather than expose his freshly detailed car to use.
concepts.serviceConnection: The clean result causes the owner to refuse the very driving he came to collect the car for. The actual service footage and spotless matching car complete the promise.
concepts.visualPayoff: The same pristine blue coupe remains in the bay as its owner calmly chooses a taxi. After the reaction, show the real foam rinse and finished clean-car footage.
concepts.risk: Without sincere performance this can sound like an ordinary booking conversation. Keep the clean finish visible and the last line natural. Do not show a different car, costume, taxi, phone UI or comic mugging.

concepts.title: Blue. Allegedly.
concepts.firstFrame: A fictional female detailer, 35, with dark hair tied back, a clean black polo and black trousers, stands beside a fictional male owner, 50, in a sage overshirt and grey T-shirt. Their sports coupe is so covered in brown road grime that its paint colour is barely visible. The expensive body shape and dirt are readable immediately; faces are close and clear above its front wing.
concepts.premise: The owner is confident about the colour of his car until the evidence beside him makes him qualify the answer. The detailer treats uncovering the paint as a perfectly routine job.
concepts.serviceConnection: The joke cannot resolve until the dirt is professionally removed. The cleaning and blue glossy result are the payoff, rather than a separate unrelated gag.
concepts.visualPayoff: A real-looking foam rinse exposes blue paint. Cut to the same dry spotless sports car with clean glass and crisp soft-light reflections.
concepts.risk: The generated dirt must genuinely obscure the paint. Inspect water contact and matching car geometry; never wipe abrasive dry grime. No artificial sparkle stars or instant morph.

dialogue.speaker: Detailer
dialogue.performance: A practical question, sincerely asked. Look at the dirt-covered paint rather than the camera.

dialogue.speaker: Detailer

concepts.title: Lost property
concepts.firstFrame: A detailer holds a single fossil-looking chip recovered from the footwell with small detailing tweezers; the owner watches as if it might be valuable.
concepts.premise: The owner cannot quite remember which takeaway the car has been preserving.
concepts.punchline: That's not mine. Mine was a salad.
concepts.serviceConnection: The recovered food is evidence of why an interior needs a proper clean. An interior vacuum and clean cabin finish the story.
concepts.visualPayoff: Spotless seat rails and footwell, with the food and accumulated debris actually removed.
concepts.risk: Too close to the rejected first film if performed as a novelty voice. Small food must be legible; it underplays the premium exterior finish requested.

dialogue.speaker: Owner
dialogue.text: That's not mine. Mine was a salad.

concepts.title: The mirror
concepts.firstFrame: A customer adjusts his hair using the deep reflection in the freshly detailed door while the waiting detailer holds his keys.
concepts.premise: The finish is sufficiently clear that the owner has started grooming himself in it.
concepts.serviceConnection: The paint finish is the visual joke. Actual cleaning coverage must establish how it was achieved.
concepts.visualPayoff: A clear, physically plausible door reflection and an immaculate complete car.
concepts.risk: Face reflections can distort in generated footage; the line relies on a visual effect that must survive phone-size review.

dialogue.speaker: Owner
dialogue.performance: Still fixing his hair, completely serious.

concepts.title: A minute for the dirt
concepts.firstFrame: The owner solemnly holds a tiny bunch of flowers beside a bucket of dirty rinse water.
concepts.premise: He treats the years of grime leaving his car as the end of a relationship.
concepts.serviceConnection: The grime leaving the car is the subject, followed by a clean-car result.
concepts.visualPayoff: The bucket is set aside and the immaculate car is revealed.
concepts.risk: The ceremony competes with the service and risks making the result feel like an afterthought. It also repeats the ceremonial mechanism of the CTN wedding.

concepts.title: Established dirt
concepts.firstFrame: The owner tries to protect a tiny weed growing out of mud on the wheel arch while a detailer prepares to clean it.
concepts.premise: The owner has become attached to what has started growing on the car.
concepts.serviceConnection: Cleaning removes the accumulated dirt, with a clear clean-wheel result.
concepts.visualPayoff: The same clean wheel arch and spotless blue paint.
concepts.risk: The plant can look fantastical and implies neglect beyond the believable audience problem. Do not buy a take merely for a large visual prop.

concepts.title: The protective suit
concepts.firstFrame: Owner in clean white disposable coveralls beside the spotless car, a practical detailer holding his keys.
concepts.premise: The owner dresses to protect the car from himself.
concepts.serviceConnection: Protecting the freshly cleaned interior becomes an excessive precaution.
concepts.visualPayoff: The immaculate cabin motivates his costume.
concepts.risk: The punchline mostly explains the costume, and the suit can read as a worker or hazardous cleaning. Independent critic declined to commission this as written.

concepts.title: Buying his own car
concepts.firstFrame: Owner admires his newly cleaned car with his wallet open.
concepts.premise: The finish makes collection feel like a showroom purchase.
concepts.serviceConnection: The car looks newly desirable after cleaning.
concepts.visualPayoff: The same clean car and its familiar keys.
concepts.risk: Repeats the recognition mechanism of Kitchen's Next. Rejected by independent review as a new direction.

creative.selectionReason: Two independent agents preferred the taxi behavioural reversal to the costume explanation. The owner makes a concrete absurd choice, then gives its service-specific justification. Ordinary clothes prevent a costume spoiling the reveal. This warrants a spoken pilot, not a claim of final quality.
